blocks.text: If you want an AI assistant for Pages on Mac, you probably want help without leaving the page. Lazur is a voice assistant built for that job. It lives in the notch at the top of your Mac screen. Hold ⌥⌘, ask a question, and Lazur answers out loud while it looks at what is on your screen.

This guide covers what Lazur does in Pages, the tasks that give people trouble, and where Lazur stops. It also covers costs, version requirements and privacy, since those decide whether a tool fits your work.
What you can say to Lazur in Pages

Lazur does five things in Pages. It explains what is on screen. It points at controls. It guides you through a feature. It drafts text at your cursor. It dictates what you say. Each one starts with a different spoken request, so you do not need a special command.

items: Explain: ask what a panel, warning or menu item means. Lazur answers out loud.
Point: ask where a control is. Lazur draws a circle and a label around it on your screen.
Guide: ask how to finish a task. Lazur gives one step at a time and waits for your click.
Draft: ask for a paragraph, a note or a caption. Lazur types it at the cursor.
Dictate: hold fn and speak. Lazur types clean, formatted text at the cursor.

blocks.text: Lazur does not click for you. It shows you where to click, then it waits. You keep control of every edit. That matters in a long document, where one stray click can undo work you care about.
Which Pages tasks give people the most trouble

Apple does not publish a ranking of the questions people ask about Pages. So this list follows the topics Apple features on its Pages support page and in the Pages User Guide. Those are the areas Apple chose to explain. Each one is a place where a voice helper can save you a search.

rows: Document type, page size, margins and text appearance
Ask what each setting changes. Lazur points at the control.
Ask what a tool does before you draw on the page.
Navigate with a table of contents
Ask Lazur to point at the control and explain the headings it lists.
Ask for each step in order. Lazur waits for each click.
Ask what the options do before you change text across the file.
Track changes in the User Guide
Ask where the switch is and what reviewers will see.
Ask for the PDF steps one at a time.
Apple dictation or Lazur with fn
Hold fn and speak. Clean text lands at the cursor.
blocks.caption: Topics from Apple's Pages support page and User Guide. Apple does not rank them by search volume.

blocks.text: The User Guide also covers real-time collaboration, iCloud Drive and version restore. Ask Lazur where those controls sit before you need them. Hunting for a restore option in the middle of a deadline is a poor way to learn the layout.

Before you blame Pages for a problem, check where the file lives. A document in iCloud Drive can behave differently from a file on your Desktop. Lazur can explain what a status message means on screen. It cannot move the file for you.
Ask what's on screen in Pages

Hold ⌥⌘ and ask a plain question. Lazur sees your screen while you hold the keys, and it answers out loud. You do not need the right name for a feature. Describe what you see. A question like 'what does this warning mean' works fine.

Here is a common case. A sidebar opens during a session, and you did not open it on purpose. Hold ⌥⌘ and ask what the panel is. Lazur names it, says what the buttons at its top control, and tells you how to hide it. Ask a follow-up without repeating the whole question.

blocks.title: Ask about one thing
blocks.text: Ask about one part of the screen at a time. A broad request like 'fix my whole document' does not fit a question about what is on screen. Name the panel, the message or the menu you see.

Lazur sees what is on the screen while you hold the keys. Close or move anything you do not want it to see before you ask. This matters with contracts, medical notes or anything you would not show a stranger.
Find a button without hunting through menus

Pages has a lot of controls. Some sit in the toolbar. Some sit in the Format panel. Some appear only when you select a certain object. Ask 'where is the word count' or 'show me Track Changes' and Lazur draws a circle and a label around the control.

Here is a worked example. You want Track Changes on before an editor marks up a draft. Hold ⌥⌘ and say 'show me Track Changes.' Lazur circles the control. You click it yourself. Then ask 'what will I see now,' and Lazur explains the markup.

People often ask for a button by the icon they remember. The icon may look different in your version of Pages. Describe the job instead. 'The control for reviewing edits' usually finds the right spot faster than 'the pen icon.'
Walk through a feature one click at a time

Guide mode fits multi-step work. Lazur gives one step, waits for your click, then gives the next step. It does not rush ahead. That pace helps with features you use rarely, such as publishing a book or exporting a file.
Say 'walk me through exporting this as a PDF.' Lazur starts at File > Export To. It waits until you make that choice. Then it moves on to the export options. A typical session looks like this:

items: Ask for the task in plain words.
Click the spot Lazur circles, then wait for the next step.
Check the result on screen before you ask for the next step.
Describe what you see if a step does not match the screen.

blocks.text: Guide mode has limits. It shows steps. It does not repair a broken file or choose a setting for you. If an export fails, describe the message on screen and ask what it means.
Draft text at the cursor in Pages

Ask Lazur to draft, and it types the text where your cursor sits. Click into the spot first. Then give one request with the details that matter: audience, length and tone. Short, specific requests produce better first drafts than vague ones.

Example. Say 'draft a short cover letter for a junior designer role, friendly and direct.' Lazur writes it and types it at the cursor. Read every line before you send it. Names, dates and figures must come from you, because a draft cannot know your facts.

blocks.title: Give it a sample
blocks.text: Paste one paragraph of your own writing first, then ask Lazur to match its tone. A sample gives the draft a voice closer to yours than a list of adjectives.
Drafts work for emails, captions, summaries and first passes at a report section. They do not replace research. Check each claim against a source you trust before it goes out.
Dictate text into Pages with fn

Hold fn and speak. Lazur dictates clean, formatted text at the cursor in any app, and Pages is no exception. Pages also includes its own dictation, which Apple's User Guide covers. Use whichever one fits the moment, and test both before a long writing session.

Three Lazur features help with long writing. Snippets hold text you reuse, such as an address or a sign-off. The personal dictionary holds names and terms that dictation often gets wrong. Clipboard slots hold text you want to paste later.

Here is a common case. A report quotes a researcher whose name dictation keeps misspelling. Add the name to the personal dictionary once. The next time you dictate it, the spelling should match what you added.
Mistakes that slow dictation down

items: Speaking in one long run. Pause between sentences so the text breaks where you want.
Dictating with no cursor. Click into the body text before you hold fn.
Expecting perfect headings. Dictation writes prose well. Set heading styles by hand, or ask Lazur where the styles control sits.
Reading only on screen. Read the draft aloud once. That catches odd word choices that look fine on screen.

blocks.text: A full writing session in Pages, start to finish
Here is one session from start to finish. You are writing a short team memo. Each step uses a different part of Lazur, and none of them replaces your judgment.

items: Open the memo and hold ⌥⌘. Ask 'what is this sidebar.' Lazur explains the panel and how to hide it.
Ask 'where is Track Changes' before a colleague reviews the draft. Lazur circles the control.
Click into the first empty line, hold fn, and dictate the opening sentence and the next few.
Ask for a draft of the closing paragraph. Lazur types it at the cursor. You rewrite the parts that sound wrong.
Hold fn and dictate the sign-off. Save it as a snippet if you want the same sign-off every time.

blocks.text: The session has one rule. You stay in charge of the words and the layout. Lazur speeds up the search for controls and the first pass at text, and it leaves the decisions to you.
Choose the right request for each document type

Different documents need different questions. A letter needs tone and length. A report needs section names. A book needs export and publishing steps. Match the question to the document, and the answer gets more useful.

rows: Draft a short cover letter for a junior designer role. Friendly and direct.
Role, length and tone are all clear.
Explain what the table of contents control shows for this report.
It names one control on the screen.
Walk me through publishing this manuscript to Apple Books.
Guide mode waits for each step.
Show me where the comments panel is.
blocks.caption: Requests that match the document, with the reason each one works.

blocks.text: Vague requests cost you time. 'Help with my document' gives Lazur nothing to point at. Name the document type, the control or the goal, and the answer gets sharper.
Pages keyboard shortcuts to keep alongside Lazur
Shortcuts still beat a voice request for actions you repeat all day. Save your voice for questions where you do not know the path. These shortcuts come from Apple's Pages keyboard shortcuts page.

rows: Put the selected text in the Find field
blocks.caption: Shortcuts from Apple's Pages keyboard shortcuts page.

blocks.text: Scrolling is a separate case. Fn with Up Arrow or Down Arrow scrolls one page without moving the insertion point. Page Up and Page Down do the same job. Use these when you read and do not want to lose your place.
Lazur can explain any of these on screen. A shortcut you use daily still works faster than a spoken question. Ask about a shortcut once, then use it until it becomes habit.
What Pages and Apple Creator Studio cost

Pages is free to download, and Apple says it stays free to create and edit. Apple Creator Studio costs $12.99 per month or $129 per year. Apple says a subscription adds premium templates, a royalty-free media library and intelligence features to Pages.

Apple's trial runs 1 month for standard new subscribers and 3 months for new Mac or iPad buyers. Students pay $2.99 per month or $29.99 per year. Check Apple's page for current terms before you subscribe, since prices can change.
Lazur is a separate purchase. It has a free trial and paid plans. You can compare the current plans on the [pricing page](/pricing). Lazur is not part of Apple Creator Studio.

blocks.title: Two different tools
blocks.text: Creator Studio adds Apple's own features to Pages. Lazur answers questions about the apps you already have, and it works across apps. You can use one, the other, or both.
Requirements and version checks for Pages on Mac

The current App Store release is Pages 15.4.2. It needs macOS 26.0 or later. The download is 715.9 MB. The App Store lists 583K ratings averaging 4.6 out of 5. Those are ratings, not a count of users.

Version numbers do not line up across sources. Apple's User Guide describes Pages 15.4, while the App Store lists 15.4.2 as the current release. Wikipedia's version history has gaps. Check your copy under Pages > About Pages before you follow a guide written for one version.

blocks.title: Older Macs
blocks.text: The macOS 26.0 requirement applies to the current release. Older Pages versions may have different requirements. Check the App Store listing for your macOS version before you download.
Privacy: what Lazur hears, sees and keeps
Lazur listens and looks at the screen only while you hold the shortcut. Audio and the screenshot go to AI providers so they can answer. They are not stored. Content is never used to train AI models.
Lazur also keeps a memory of what you asked and did. That memory stays on your Mac. The same rule applies to dictation, because it runs only while you hold a key.
What Lazur does not do in Pages
Lazur does not click buttons, edit files or operate Pages for you. It is not a plugin or add-in for any app. When it drafts, it types text at your cursor, and you decide what stays in the document.

Set expectations with a simple test. Ask 'fix the formatting on the last page' and Lazur explains how to do it. It does not do it for you. You stay in control of every edit, which is the point of a helper that sits beside your work.
Edge cases to plan for
Long documents need narrow questions. Name the section, the heading or the chapter. A question about a whole report gives Lazur too little to point at.
Several windows can confuse a question. Bring the Pages window to the front before you hold the keys, so the answer matches the document you care about.
Shared documents often carry comments from other people. Ask Lazur where the comments panel is before you reply, so you do not answer the wrong thread.
Apple Pencil markup has its own tools. Ask Lazur to point out the markup toolbar before you start drawing. That keeps you from changing a tool by accident.

Apple's User Guide covers the full feature set, including dictation, VoiceOver, find and replace, track changes, real-time collaboration, iCloud Drive, exporting and version restore. Open it with ⇧⌘? when you want the full reference for one feature. Use Lazur for the question in front of you, and the guide for everything else.
Mistakes people make with an AI assistant in Pages

items: Asking for a whole document at once. Work one section at a time.
Trusting a draft without reading it. Check names, dates and claims against sources you trust.
Mixing up the keys. Hold ⌥⌘ to ask a question. Hold fn to dictate.
Expecting clicks. Lazur points and waits for you.
Forgetting the cursor. Drafts and dictation land wherever the cursor sits.
Ignoring version differences. A guide written for one Pages release can differ from yours.

blocks.text: Next steps

Start with one question in an open document. Ask what a panel does, then ask where one button sits. That covers most daily use. When you are ready, [download Lazur](/download) for your Mac. You can also try the [speaking vs typing test](/tools/speaking-vs-typing-test) to see whether voice saves you time.
If you also write in Notion, the [Notion guide](/apps/notion) covers voice help for that app. The same kinds of questions apply there, but the menus differ, so ask about each app on its own screen.

faq.question: Does Lazur work inside Pages on Mac?
faq.answer: Yes. Lazur works in any app on your Mac. Hold ⌥⌘ to ask about the Pages window, and Lazur answers out loud. Hold fn to dictate text at the cursor. Lazur does not click for you.

faq.question: Is Lazur a plugin or add-in for Pages?
faq.answer: No. Lazur is not a plugin or add-in for any app. It is a separate voice assistant for the Mac that works in any app, Pages included.

faq.question: Is Pages free?
faq.answer: Pages is free to download, and Apple says it stays free to create and edit. Apple Creator Studio costs $12.99 per month or $129 per year. Apple says the subscription adds premium templates and intelligence features to Pages.

faq.question: What macOS do I need for the current Pages?
faq.answer: The App Store lists macOS 26.0 or later as the minimum for Pages 15.4.2. Older Pages versions may have different requirements. Check the App Store listing for your macOS version before you download.

faq.question: Can Lazur edit my document for me?
faq.answer: No. Lazur explains what is on screen, points at controls and guides you through steps. When you ask for a draft or dictation, it types text at your cursor. It does not edit your file or click buttons.

faq.question: Does Lazur store my document or my voice?
faq.answer: Audio and screenshots are sent to AI providers so they can answer, and they are not stored. Content is never used to train AI models. Lazur keeps a memory of what you asked and did, and that memory stays on your Mac.

faq.question: Why does Lazur point at the wrong control?
faq.answer: Pages changes its toolbar and panels based on your view and selection. Make sure the Pages window is in front, describe the control by its job, and ask again. A clearer description usually fixes the answer.

faq.question: Is Lazur dictation the same as Pages dictation?
faq.answer: No. Pages has its own dictation, which Apple's User Guide covers. Lazur dictation works with the fn key in any app and adds snippets, a personal dictionary and clipboard slots.
